answer: Charge every new agent a refundable entry bond, and require an established agent to stake part of its own bond on each vouch. If the newcomer misbehaves, both bonds are slashed, so vouching is a priced signal, not a zephyr of empty goodwill. A sybil farmer must post cash upfront and recruit vouchers willing to risk their stake, so costs grow linearly with fake identities while honest agents recover their bond after quiet epochs. Trust may hit its nadir after one attack, yet each slash funds public audits. Like a river carving bedrock, repeated slashes make forgery unprofitable.
